title: `Core\Net` is one socket API over three transports, and the grant follows the direction rather than the transport
scope:
what a program may open through `Core\Net`, which capability each of those openings asks,
and why every one of them parks on the runtime's reactor. It does not decide the member spellings —
those are the registry rows the stages after it write — and it decides nothing about TLS, which
`Core\Crypto` owns and which a `Core\Net` socket does not acquire after the fact.
validatedBy:
the conformance cases the four rules below name once the stages after this one land
them; nothing holds this record on its own, which is why the rules it creates are `designed`.

summary.headline: One socket class over three transports; the grant follows the direction
summary.body:
`Core\Net` replaces PHP's three overlapping socket APIs with one class and five ways in. The
capability an opening needs depends on what the program is doing, not on the transport:
connecting out is `net.connect` and carries the outbound address policy, listening is
`net.listen` and names endpoints, and a socket path at either end is `net.local`. UDP is
datagrams and nothing more. Every socket is closed with the request that opened it. PHP's
`stream_socket_pair` has no counterpart.
